- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and model overestimates, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior 3-day avg), model tends to overreact; cap forecast peak at 2–3% above prior high.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.00), model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply +0.8–1.2% bias to first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated positive signals, model tends to lag; delay forecast peak by 1–2 days and adjust upward by 0.5–1.0%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts late period (days 20–30) — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% in final 5 days if sentiment is flat or negative.
